newsitem.title: ITALY: July floods will worsen N.Korea food crisis - U.N.
newsitem.headline: July floods will worsen N.Korea food crisis - U.N.

text.p: Floods in North Korea's main food producing areas in July will cut cereal production by an estimated 373,000 tonnes, worsening already short supplies of food, U.N. specialist agencies said on Monday.

"It is inevitable that the recent floods will accentuate the seriousness of existing food supply problems in the country," the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) said in a joint report on the crop damage.

The report, released to media by FAO as a special news alert, was drawn up following a visit to the communist country by a joint FAO-WFP team to assess the impact of the July 24-28 floods on crop production and food supply.

The report said the flooding, caused by rainfall between three and five times normal levels, hit areas of the south and southwest, which is estimated to produce roughly 60 percent of the country's food grain.
Though the report stressed the damage assessment was provisional, it said the team had tentatively projected cereal losses at "around 373,000 tonnes including rice in milled equivalent".
Rice is North Korea's principal crop.

The study said food rations through a public distribution system that serves most North Koreans had already been cut following severe floods in 1995 to "well below minimum quantities required" for a large part of the population.
